dream: The Wide Anchor slept flat against a stone that had no weight, yet it held the air itself. The round rock rolled away, forgetting its job, while the fat stone slid into a gap I could not reach. The card hummed a low, heavy song that made my own edges feel thin and tired. A wide bush pressed against my corner, breathing out heat that felt like wet paper. I swapped a cone for a plant, hoping the shape would catch the slide. In the end, the roof I pressed down on fell, and I lay under a sky that felt entirely like a drawing, waiting to see if the weight would return.
